content.title: What is String Transformation?
content.description: String Transformation refers to modifying a string from one form to another through operations such as replacement, conversion, formatting, compression, or rearrangement.

content.content: Modern applications constantly transform strings. Whether converting text to uppercase, formatting dates, encoding URLs, encrypting messages, or compressing files, string transformation plays a critical role in software systems.

content.title: Real-World Importance
content.content: Every email, website URL, QR code, password hash, and data transmission relies on some form of string transformation or encoding.
Common String Transformations

items.question: Case Conversion
items.answer: Convert text between uppercase and lowercase.

content.content: Case Transformation
Case transformation changes character casing while preserving content. This is frequently used in search engines, data validation, and text normalization.
Character Replacement
Character replacement modifies specific characters or words within a string. It is commonly used in content filtering, text processing, and data cleaning applications.

content.title: Industry Usage
content.content: Text editors and word processors use replacement operations extensively for search-and-replace features.
String Encoding
Encoding converts text into a specific format that computers can store, transmit, and interpret correctly across different systems.

content.title: Why Encoding Matters
content.description: Without encoding standards, different devices could interpret the same data differently, causing corruption or unreadable text.

content.content: ASCII Encoding
ASCII is one of the earliest character encoding standards. It assigns numerical values to letters, digits, and symbols.

content.title: ASCII Limitation
content.content: ASCII supports only 128 characters and cannot represent most world languages.
Unicode & UTF-8
Unicode was developed to support characters from virtually every language. UTF-8 is the most widely used Unicode encoding standard today.
Run-Length Encoding (RLE)
Run-Length Encoding is a simple compression technique that stores repeated characters using counts instead of repeating the character multiple times.

content.title: Where RLE is Used
content.content: Simple image formats and data compression systems often use Run-Length Encoding.
URL Encoding
URLs cannot contain certain special characters directly. URL encoding converts these characters into a safe format for web transmission.

content.title: Why URL Encoding?
content.description: Web browsers and servers require a standardized format for transmitting special characters through URLs.

content.content: Base64 Encoding
Base64 converts binary data into readable text using a set of 64 characters. It is widely used for transmitting images, files, and tokens.

content.title: Important Clarification
content.content: Base64 is an encoding technique, not an encryption method. It does not provide security.
Encoding vs Encryption
Applications of String Encoding

items.question: Mobile Apps
items.answer: Data exchange between devices and servers.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Language Translation
content.content: Encoding is similar to translating a message into a universal language that everyone can understand. Different devices may speak different 'languages', but encoding ensures they communicate correctly.

content.title: Interesting Fact
content.content: UTF-8 powers the modern internet and supports over 95% of all websites worldwide.
Common Mistakes

items.question: What is the most common misconception?
items.answer: Believing encoding and encryption are the same thing.

items.question: Why does text appear corrupted?
items.answer: Different systems use incompatible encoding formats.

items.question: Why is Unicode preferred?
items.answer: It supports global languages and symbols.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Questions involving compression, character encoding, URL conversion, Base64, or Unicode often test understanding of string transformation concepts.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: String transformation modifies text into another form.
Encoding ensures consistent storage and transmission.
UTF-8 is the most common encoding standard.
Base64 converts binary data into text.
Encoding and encryption are not the same.
